method: Manual diff and source control/data dependency review; exact wrapper inverse module/instance rename checked by bytes
findings: Each of64 constant owner lanes applies release then descriptors0..3 then body DWORDs0..3 and bytes0..3; later same-ID writes see all earlier updates, as in v1.

Per-entry error starts0 and is only set, then OR-reduced with unchanged global descriptor order/exclusivity and empty-DWORD checks before any state commit. Errors cannot be erased by a later same-ID update.
Four literal raw destinations match old received<4 variable slice; received==8191 is diagnosed before increment wraps. Error halts and clears event count rather than committing candidate state.
Ordered event gather reads final per-entry next state; readiness/release uses registered state and old held event only, with no new combinational feedback path identified.
Header/FC decode, complete6-bit owner space, epoch/flush, held-event and TLP atomic fork logic are unchanged. Wrapper is byte-identical after the two explicit names are restored.
The earlier external abort same-edge repair remains in inherited wrapper flush; v1 failure evidence is separate and preserved.
limitations: No formal functional equivalence or timing proof
No all-parameter or malformed untrusted upstream protocol qualification
Trusted owned CRC-qualified upstream remains the boundary; decoded events do not themselves implement a controller
